# Audit Scope & Completeness Checklist: Plugin Prefix Audit

**Purpose**: Validate that the audit's scope, classification rules, and remediation requirements are complete, clear, unambiguous, and ready for a PR reviewer to sign off on before the audit report is treated as authoritative
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean the audit itself (findings/report) has been produced or is correct.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all file types the audit must cover explicitly enumerated (PHP, JS, SCSS, JSON, pattern files), with no format left implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
  - Satisfied: FR-001 requires "every file under the repository" (not a restricted list), which is stronger than an explicit format enumeration — no format is left implicit.
- [x] CHK002 Are the directories/paths excluded from the audit (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `.git`, build output) exhaustively listed rather than left to interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Edge Cases]
  - Satisfied: `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.git`, build output are named in FR-001 and Edge Cases; research.md and plan.md additionally name `dist` explicitly.
- [x] CHK003 Is the full set of default-prefix case/format variants to search for specified, rather than relying on a single canonical spelling? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
  - Satisfied: Assumptions lists five variants explicitly (`example-plugin`, `Example_Plugin`, `EXAMPLE_PLUGIN`, `example_plugin`, `ExamplePlugin`).
- [x] CHK004 Are the required fields for an "unreplaced" finding (path, excerpt, risk, remediation) each individually specified as mandatory? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
  - Satisfied: FR-003 lists all four fields, and data-model.md's validation rules make `risk`/`remediation` explicitly mandatory for `unreplaced` findings.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Is the boundary between "intentional" and "unreplaced" classification defined with concrete criteria (e.g. specific directories/file roles), rather than left to reviewer judgment alone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]
  - Resolved: FR-002 now states the concrete directory-level rule directly (`tests/`, `scripts/`, `.github/schemas/examples/`, onboarding docs = intentional; `inc/`, `src/`, `patterns/`, etc. = unreplaced), folded back from research.md into the spec itself.
- [x] CHK006 Is "area/component" grouping defined with a fixed, enumerable set of categories rather than an open-ended taxonomy? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
  - Satisfied: FR-004's examples are non-exhaustive ("e.g."), but data-model.md's `area` field pins it to a fixed enum (`php-core`, `js-build-tooling`, `scss`, `json-config-schema`, `patterns`, `docs-other`).
- [x] CHK007 Is it unambiguous whether the audit report is the sole deliverable, or whether remediation (actual code changes) is also expected in this change? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
  - Resolved: FR-007's hedge was removed. It now states definitively that remediation is out of scope for this change and is tracked as separate follow-up items.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK008 Do the audit checklist items required by FR-006 match, one-to-one, the checklist items named in the LS-3726 issue template? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
  - Resolved: FR-006 now explicitly accounts for all 8 LS-3726 checklist items — 5 as audit-content items in this FR's scope, and the remaining 3 (PR description, changelog, labels) explicitly named as PR-process items out of this FR's scope but still covered elsewhere (tasks T016/T018). No longer a partial, unexplained match.
- [x] CHK009 Are the "intentional" classification criteria in the spec/assumptions consistent with how test fixtures and generator scripts are treated elsewhere in the requirements (no contradiction between FR-002 and the Assumptions section)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]
  - Satisfied: FR-002's categories and the Assumptions section describe the same intentional/unreplaced split with no contradiction.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK010 Can SC-001 ("100% of files... accounted for") be objectively verified without re-interpreting what counts as "accounted for"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
  - Satisfied: data-model.md's validation rule ("every Finding MUST have a classification") gives "accounted for" a concrete, checkable meaning.
- [x] CHK011 Is SC-004 ("act on any remediation item using only the audit report") testable by a reviewer who was not involved in producing the report? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
  - Resolved: SC-004 now names a concrete verification step (a PR reviewer explicitly confirming, in the PR review, that they could identify risk/remediation from the report alone) rather than an unverifiable subjective claim.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for how partial-word/substring matches of the default prefix (false positives inside unrelated identifiers) should be handled? [Edge Case, Gap]
  - Resolved: new FR-002a requires a complete-token match; substring-only matches are false positives, excluded from findings, and noted once in the report's Scope section.
- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for what happens if a file is ambiguous (plausibly either intentional or unreplaced) and the audit cannot confidently classify it? [Coverage, Gap]
  - Resolved: new FR-002b introduces a third classification, "needs-review," with a required ambiguity note, instead of forcing a binary choice.
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for documentation/README files that intentionally demonstrate the default prefix for onboarding, distinct from source files? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
  - Satisfied: FR-002's "documentation example" category and the Edge Cases entry on onboarding docs both address this directly.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK015 Is the assumption that generator/test-fixture references are "intentional unless the generator itself fails to replace them" validated anywhere, or left as an unverified assumption? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
  - Resolved: the Assumptions section no longer asserts unverified generator correctness as fact. It now explicitly states that verifying the generator's replacement behavior is out of scope for this audit and would require a separate follow-up — a deliberate scope decision, not a silent unverified claim.
- [x] CHK016 Is the audit report's committed location (`.github/spec/001-plugin-prefix-audit/audit-report.md`) treated as a firm requirement or still an open decision deferred to planning? [Traceability, Spec §FR-005, Plan Structure Decision]
  - Satisfied: FR-005 only says "e.g., an audit report document," but plan.md's Structure Decision fixes the exact path, and tasks.md (T001) builds against that fixed path.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
